name: paid-memberships-pro
notes: Production-readiness audit 2026-08-22: the official upstream Paid Memberships Pro 3.8.3 tag artifact is pinned at SHA-256 6c3acc683939e01f203037334c16dddd146aaa30e01e09c41c6503705c1db7bf. The one-patch range admits only those inspected bytes; widening requires a new schema, lifecycle, reference, deletion, and plugin-behavior exercise.

Grind R3-B (task #91). PLUGIN-SOURCING FINDING, worth recording since it changes the task brief's own premise: Paid Memberships Pro was PERMANENTLY removed from the wp.org plugin directory on 2024-10-17 (author's own request; they now self-host distribution after a dispute with Automattic/Matt Mullenweg over control of the wp.org listing) — `wp plugin install paid-memberships-pro` fails with 'closed'. Still genuinely free/GPLv2 and officially maintained at github.com/strangerstudios/paid-memberships-pro; this manifest and its grind fixture were built against the official release tag 3.8.3, installed via `wp plugin install https://github.com/strangerstudios/paid-memberships-pro/archive/refs/tags/3.8.3.zip --activate` (wp-cli auto-detects the GitHub source and renames the extracted folder to the clean `paid-memberships-pro` slug). A real-world consequence worth flagging for DESIGN.md's own code-half story: PMPro is now a 'free but not wp.org' plugin, a middle case between the wp.org-composer path and the fully premium/vendored `code/wp-content/plugins/` path DESIGN.md section 3's site-repo layout already anticipates for exactly this kind of plugin.

SECOND premise correction: the task brief's shorthand 'pmpro_pages option = a serialized map of page ids' does not match this version's real schema. There is no `pmpro_pages` option at all. PMPro's system pages (account/billing/cancel/checkout/confirmation/invoice/levels/login/member_profile_edit) are each their OWN individual option, `pmpro_<name>_page_id`, holding one plain numeric page id directly (confirmed by reading includes/init.php, where the request-scoped PHP global `$pmpro_pages` array is assembled at runtime FROM these nine options — the array is a runtime convenience, never itself persisted). This is simpler to classify than the brief's assumption: nine ordinary `{"class": "authored", "ref": "post"}` option rules, the exact same shape manifests/woocommerce.json already uses for `woocommerce_checkout_page_id` etc. — no json_refs/key_refs structured-value handling needed at all. Pages are created via the plugin's own real API, `pmpro_generatePages()` (includes/functions.php) — the same function both the Setup Wizard (adminpages/wizard/save-steps.php) and the 'Settings > Pages' admin screen's 'create missing pages' button call — used directly in this round's seed, not hand-rolled.

THIRD correction: the brief's 'pmpro_memberships_users/pmpro_orders = runtime' shorthand names the wrong table for orders — the real table is `pmpro_membership_orders` (DESCRIBE'd live; there is no bare `pmpro_orders`). Classified runtime below, alongside its `pmpro_membership_ordermeta` EAV sidecar (also runtime, since Snapshot.php's meta_tables_by_owner() requires an authored_snapshot_meta table's attached_to.table to itself be an authored_snapshot table — a runtime owner makes its sidecar structurally ineligible for anything but a plain runtime marker too, mirroring manifests/ninja-forms.json's nf3_object_meta/nf3_relationships treatment of NF's own runtime-owned sidecars).

pmpro_membership_levels (the primary authored_snapshot fixture this round): DESCRIBE'd live — id (PK, auto_increment) plus 13 plain scalar columns, ZERO FK-shaped columns of its own. Identity: mapped, not natural_key — verified empirically that `name` carries no uniqueness constraint at the DB level (`SHOW CREATE TABLE` / DESCRIBE: a plain MUL index, not UNIQUE) AND no application-layer duplicate check either (read adminpages/levels/save-level.php, the real admin save handler behind 'Add New Level': it calls `pmpro_insert_or_replace()` unconditionally, no name-collision guard anywhere in the path) — unlike manifests/woocommerce.json's `attribute_name` (WooCommerce's OWN create path DOES refuse a duplicate there), PMPro's `name` is genuinely just a text field a site builder could duplicate by accident, so claiming natural_key stability here would be dishonest. Every column classified authored (site-builder pricing/policy config: name/description/confirmation text, initial_payment/billing_amount/cycle_number/cycle_period/billing_limit/trial_amount/trial_limit — the recurring-billing shape, expiration_number/expiration_period, allow_signups). `allow_signups` declared lint_ok true proactively (a 0/1 flag of the exact shape manifests/ninja-forms.json's BIT(1) columns and this round's own TEC _EventShowMap/_EventShowMapLink findings already established WILL eventually coincide with a small entity id). `cycle_number`/`expiration_number` (both small human-entered 'how many' counts — billing cadence and expiration length) DID trip `wp duo lint`'s bare_id check live on this round's own two-level fixture (value 1, coinciding with post id 1) — reviewed and confirmed genuinely not refs, lint_ok added reactively. `billing_limit`/`trial_limit` are the identical species (confirmed via adminpages/levels/save-level.php: all four are `intval($_REQUEST[...])` reads of a plain numeric admin form field, nothing FK-shaped about any of them) but happened to be 0 on both of this round's levels (0 never coincides with a real id, so lint never tripped on them) — lint_ok added proactively for the same reason manifests/ninja-forms.json marks a whole BIT(1) COLUMN rather than chasing today's specific collision: the exemption is about the column's structural value space, not this round's particular numbers.

pmpro_membership_levelmeta — ATTEMPTED as a genuine authored_snapshot_meta declaration, and it is EXACTLY where THIS round's third distinct engine gap was found (not the composite-PK gap — a different one): agent/src/Repository/Snapshot.php's assert_meta_schema() HARDCODES the literal string 'id' into its own expected-columns set (`$expected = array_unique(array_filter(['id', $attachCol, $keyCol, $valCol, ...]))`) with no manifest field anywhere to override it — confirmed by reading the function, then confirmed the hard way, live: declaring this table threw `attached-meta table 'pmpro_membership_levelmeta' schema mismatch — expected columns [id, meta_key, meta_value, pmpro_membership_level_id], found [meta_id, meta_key, meta_value, pmpro_membership_level_id]`. DESCRIBE'd live, the real PK column here is `meta_id`, not `id` (nf3_*_meta's own PK genuinely IS named `id` — manifests/ninja-forms.json's declarations happened to never need an override, which is presumably why this was never noticed before: the hardcoding was invisible until a SECOND plugin's meta table used a different PK column name, exactly the kind of foreign-schema stress this round's brief asked for). No workaround exists at the manifest level — the column name is baked into engine code this round's mandate forbids editing (agent/src/ is off-limits; ≤10-line obviously-correct fixes are the only sanctioned exception, and adding a new manifest-driven field with a default requires touching both Snapshot.php's assert_meta_schema() AND its capture/apply read sites, past that bar). Downgraded to the pre-existing honest-intent marker instead of a real declaration; characterized as an engine gap with acceptance criteria (an `id_column` field, defaulting to `'id'` for exact backward compatibility with the nf3_*/attribute_taxonomies fixtures, overridable like `key_column`/`value_column` already are) and escalated to team-lead from grind round R3-B. Two real keys were confirmed empirically before this gap was hit (worth recording even though uncaptured): `confirmation_in_email` (0/1 toggle) and `membership_account_message` (free text), both written by the real save-level.php admin handler, both genuinely authored, both site-builder-configured in this round's own fixture.

THE SECOND MAJOR FINDING OF THIS ROUND — a composite-primary-key join table has NO REPRESENTATION in the typed-snapshot grammar at all, confirmed by reading agent/src/Repository/Snapshot.php's assert_row_schema() directly (not inferred): `$pk = (string) ($decl['pk'] ?? '')` reads and stores exactly ONE column name, later cast straight to `(int) $row[$pk]` as the row's scalar local_id for the duo_map ledger lookup — there is no path for a MULTI-column primary key anywhere in this file. `pmpro_memberships_pages` (membership_id, page_id) — DESCRIBE'd live: a composite PK, NO surrogate id column exists at all — is exactly this shape, and it is the table that genuinely matters most in this round's scenario: it is PMPro's real content-restriction mechanism (confirmed by reading includes/metaboxes.php's `pmpro_page_save()` -> includes/functions.php's `pmpro_update_post_level_restrictions()`, the exact code path behind the real wp-admin 'Require Membership' meta box on a page/post edit screen — driven directly in this round's seed, not hand-rolled SQL). This round's 'Studio Members Only' page IS restricted to the 'Studio Access' level for real (verified: a fresh visitor gets PMPro's real restriction message; the member created in this round can access it — see the grind report's render-check section) — a genuine authored fact this manifest cannot capture at all today. `pmpro_memberships_categories` (membership_id, category_id — PMPro's OTHER restriction mechanism, category-wide rather than per-page, also surfaced in save-level.php via `pmpro_updateMembershipCategories()`) and `pmpro_discount_codes_levels` (code_id, level_id — which levels a discount code applies to, with its own per-level price overrides) share the identical composite-PK shape and the identical gap. All three are marked with the pre-existing honest-intent marker (`authored_typed_snapshot_post_v1`) rather than a real declaration — characterized as an engine gap with acceptance criteria (either a composite-key identity mode whose ordered column tuple derives the ledger's own key — as a deterministic string composite, or as a natural_key-style uuid derived straight from the tuple — or an explicit join-table class carrying no per-row uuid at all, reconciled as an owned edge-set the way authored_snapshot_meta sidecars already are, since a join row has no independent existence to identify), escalated to team-lead from grind round R3-B, not forced.

pmpro_discount_codes / pmpro_groups / pmpro_membership_levels_groups: DIFFERENT situation from the three composite-PK tables above, and the notes are careful to keep the two apart. Each of these DOES have a normal single-column surrogate `id` PK (DESCRIBE'd live) and is therefore structurally capturable via the existing authored_snapshot grammar in principle — but none was exercised with real content this round (this scenario's two membership levels needed no discount codes or level-groups to satisfy task #91's brief), so declaring full column-by-column grammar for them would claim a round-trip proof this round never performed, the same discipline grind round R1-B's shipping-zone tables already established ('don't declare more than intent-markers for untested tables, even schema-known ones'). Marked with the same honest-intent marker as the composite-PK tables, but for the OPPOSITE reason: not attempted, not blocked.

pmpro_memberships_users / pmpro_membership_orders / pmpro_membership_ordermeta / pmpro_subscriptions / pmpro_subscriptionmeta / pmpro_discount_codes_uses / pmpro_email_log: all runtime. Confirmed live for the primary one this round's brief calls out: a real member signup (`pmpro_changeMembershipLevel()`, the plugin's own real enrollment function — used internally by checkout completion and commonly by imports/manual admin enrollment) on side 1 produced a real `pmpro_memberships_users` row for a real new WP user, and stays side-1-local through the round's runtime-isolation check.

options: this version's PMPro introduced NO post_meta keys anywhere in this round's scenario (membership levels are table rows, not post meta; restriction is the join table above; system pages are ordinary WP pages with nothing PMPro-specific attached) — this manifest's post_meta section is deliberately empty, not an oversight.

pmpro_restricted_files_random_string: classified env on SEMANTIC grounds (its own option name states its purpose: a per-install random string for obfuscating protected-file download URLs — DESIGN.md's own 'salts are the canonical env-bound case' applies regardless of whether the automated secret-heuristic's entropy threshold happens to fire on this specific 10-character value) — a deliberate human override of what the heuristic tier alone might miss, the same 'proposal is advisory, never authority' posture grind round R1-A's own `secret_key` finding already established.

pmpro_gateway_environment / pmpro_last_known_url: env — the former is literally PMPro's own sandbox-vs-live payment gateway toggle (an environment distinction by definition); the latter tracks THIS install's own detected URL, env-bound like siteurl.

The nine pmpro_*_page_id options + pmpro_tospage (a legacy, currently-unused Terms-of-Service page reference predating some of the newer page-ref options, confirmed empty on this fixture) are all `ref: post` — the option_ref_tokens null-safe path (already proven on `wp_page_for_privacy_policy` in Spike A) handles pmpro_tospage's empty/unset value the same way.

DUO-3235 (both engine gaps from this round now closed): pmpro_membership_levelmeta and pmpro_memberships_pages are real declarations below, no longer honest-intent markers. Re-DESCRIBE'd live against the SAME 3.8.3 tag on a fresh sandbox pair before writing these (empirics before classification, not trusting the earlier notes' memory): pmpro_membership_levelmeta is meta_id(PK,auto_increment)/pmpro_membership_level_id/meta_key/meta_value — exactly as this file's own earlier note recorded, now declared with the new `id_column` field (agent/src/Repository/Snapshot.php's assert_meta_schema()/capture_meta_rows()/reconcile_meta() previously hardcoded the literal string 'id' at THREE call sites, not just the one that happened to throw first — see Snapshot.php's own docblock). pmpro_memberships_pages carries a THIRD live column beyond the composite PK that this file's earlier note never mentioned: `modified TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp() ON UPDATE current_timestamp()` — an auto-maintained MySQL column, never authored, classified runtime below (accounted for via an ordinary `columns{}` entry — the new identity.mode=composite_ref schema assertion still enforces 'every live column classified,' same as every other row table). `pmpro_memberships_categories` shares the identical 3-column shape (membership_id/category_id/modified, DESCRIBE'd live) and is now structurally capturable via the same composite_ref grammar in principle — left as the honest-intent marker anyway, matching this file's own `pmpro_discount_codes`/`pmpro_groups` precedent just above: not attempted with real content this round (no category-restriction fact was seeded), so not claimed. `pmpro_discount_codes_levels` is a DIFFERENT, harder case even now: composite `(code_id, level_id)` PK PLUS nine real pricing-override columns (initial_payment/billing_amount/cycle_number/cycle_period/billing_limit/trial_amount/trial_limit/expiration_number/expiration_period, DESCRIBE'd live) — composite_ref's grammar has a place for genuine extra authored columns on a composite-identity table (finalize_composite_row() upserts them), but again unexercised with real content this round, so it stays a marker too.

DUO-3232: every exact env-classified option below carries the mandatory `required` flag (Policy::validate_env_options()). Payment selection, sandbox/live mode, credentials, webhook/connect identifiers, anti-spam credentials, license state, URL/SSL state, and optional integration switches are all target-owned. They are `required: false` because PMPro supports free levels and multiple mutually-exclusive gateways: no unconditional manifest rule can honestly require one gateway's values on every target. A configured operator can provision the selected target gateway through env-set; an unconfigured free-level site remains valid.

Production-readiness closure 2026-08-23: the admitted range is the two inspected official tags 3.8.2 and 3.8.3, whose PMPro table schema is byte-identical; exact clean installs and the supported in-place 3.8.2-to-3.8.3 upgrade are exercised from SHA-256-pinned upstream archives. Official adjacent tags 3.8.1 and 3.8.4 are refusal fixtures. Five former intent-only tables are now real declarations: discount codes use their plugin-enforced unique code as natural identity; groups and the level-group edge keep mapped surrogate identity because PMPro permits duplicate names and the edge has its own id; discount-level and category restrictions use composite references. Parent level, discount-code, and group deletion stays unsupported because PMPro runtime memberships/orders/uses and extension-owned references make the reverse-reference boundary open; only the four pure authored edge rows have positive deletion authority.

The membership-level EAV keyspace is closed to the five keys written or consumed by the exact free artifact: confirmation_in_email, membership_account_message, enable_avatars, stripe_product_id, and stripe_product_id_sandbox. The first three are authored; the Stripe product ids are environment-owned remote identifiers and never enter canonical state. A later core or add-on key refuses at the keyspace gate rather than inheriting an authored default. Provider paid-memberships-pro-cache clears and independently reads back the exact PMPro object-cache group used by get_metadata() after SQL materialization, including persistent object-cache installations; it does not flush unrelated cache groups.

PMPro's pmpro_user_fields_settings option stores nested stdClass objects. Duo's portable-state contract intentionally rejects PHP object payloads, and there is no plugin API that losslessly exports and imports that graph as plain data at these tags. That optional custom-checkout-field surface remains a loud unsupported boundary, as do add-on-created options/tables/meta. Every credential and remote integration identifier named by the exact free artifacts is explicitly environment-owned so capture can proceed on a configured payment site without copying or logging those values; core email-template option patterns are bounded to the artifact's exact built-in template slugs so add-on templates still refuse.
